# Appeal of Denial — Rotator Cuff Repair (CPT 29827)

**RE:** Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
**Member:** Riley Foster
**Member ID:** W204716433
**Reference number:** POC-D5606CAED3-36942
**Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-22
**Governing policy cited by plan:** eviCore CMM-315 Shoulder Surgery - Arthroscopic and Open Procedures (https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2025-02/EviCore_CMM-315%20Shoulder%20Surg%20Arthro_Final_V1.0.2025_Pub02.25.2025.pdf), effective 2025-07-01

Dear Banner Health Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for my rotator cuff repair surgery (CPT 29827), which my plan denied in the notice dated 2026-08-22. I am requesting a full reconsideration of this decision.

## Why I am appealing

The denial notice states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I do not agree with this conclusion, and I am asking the plan to review the record again.

## What the record shows

My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this surgery is medically necessary. The record submitted with the prior authorization request includes the following:

- **Imaging:** An MRI of the shoulder performed on 2026-07-06 showed a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy.
- **Duration and severity of symptoms:** I have had 18 months of progressive shoulder pain that has not improved with rest.
- **Conservative treatment already tried and failed:** I completed 24 visits of supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics over 10 weeks (2026-04-17 to 2026-06-26), as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. I also took NSAIDs for 4 months without adequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-21 that gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.
- **Functional limitation:** I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height or sleep on the affected side.
- **Exam findings:** Provocative testing on the affected side was positive, and my range of motion is limited by pain.
- **No confounding conditions:** There is no active infection or untreated substance use noted in my chart.

## About the specific plan criteria

I want to be transparent with the reviewer: the policy excerpts made available to me for this appeal are drawn from the sections of eviCore CMM-315 addressing labral repair, biceps tenodesis, shoulder instability/laxity surgery, and capsular release/manipulation under anesthesia. For example, the policy states that "Labral repair is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:" and lists specific orthopedic tests, function-limiting pain, and "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months duration." None of the excerpts I have been given set out the specific medical-necessity criteria that eviCore CMM-315 applies to rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827) itself, so I am not able to quote the exact rotator cuff repair criteria back to the plan.

What I can say, based on the record above, is that my case independently satisfies the pattern of medical-necessity elements the policy applies elsewhere in this same document to other shoulder procedures: imaging showing a structural tear correlated with my reported symptoms and exam findings, function-limiting pain that interferes with ordinary activities (I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height or sleep on the affected side), and documented failure of provider-directed non-surgical management well beyond three months (10 weeks of supervised PT, 4 months of NSAIDs, and a corticosteroid injection).

I am asking the plan to identify and apply the specific rotator cuff repair criteria within its own eviCore CMM-315 policy, and to explain, with reference to that language, how my MRI findings and clinical record fail to meet it. If the plan believes the imaging is inadequate, I would ask that it specify what additional imaging finding or correlation is required under its own policy.

## What I am requesting

I ask that the plan reverse this denial and approve coverage for the rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827) recommended by Dr. Okafor. If the plan is not able to approve the request on this record, I ask that it identify precisely which criterion in eviCore CMM-315 has not been met and provide the specific policy language, so that my surgeon and I can respond directly to that requirement.

Please treat this letter as my formal appeal. I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-18. I will send it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, or, if that is not available to me, I will call the number on the back of my insurance card to confirm where member appeals are filed.

Please let me know if any additional information is needed to complete this review.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Riley Foster
Member ID: W204716433
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Date: [date of signature]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
